units.title: Basics: jobs and Burst
units.blurb: Two separate things — threads and a compiler, what Burst can and cannot compile, the kinds of jobs and Schedule versus Run versus Complete. This is where they check you have really used them.

units.title: Data, safety and dependencies
units.blurb: How data gets into a job and back, the safety system and races, the dependency graph, allocators and leaks, writing from a parallel job and batchSize. This is where mid-levels drop out.

units.title: Deeper: how Burst makes code fast
units.blurb: Vectorization and the Burst Inspector, SoA versus AoS, float determinism, debugging Burst, FunctionPointer and SharedStatic, transforms and physics from jobs, and when Burst is not worth it.

units.title: Entities and how to answer at the interview
units.blurb: Entities on top of Jobs and Burst, structural changes and sync points, the hybrid with GameObjects and honest limits, and how to talk about your own experience so they recognise one of their own.
